target_moa.text: Decitabine is incorporated into DNA after phosphorylation and inhibits DNA methyltransferase, causing hypomethylation of DNA and cellular differentiation or apoptosis; it is also cytotoxic as an S-phase specific agent.

citations.quote: Decitabine is believed to exert its antineoplastic effects after phosphorylation and direct incorporation into DNA and inhibition of DNA methyltransferase, causing hypomethylation of DNA and cellular differentiation or apoptosis.

DAC is sequentially phosphorylated to mono-, di-, and triphosphate, which is incorporated into DNA in place of deoxycytidine and binds covalently to DNA methyltransferases, thereby inhibiting DNA methylation. DAC-containing DNA is also cytotoxic as an S-phase specific agent to proliferating cells.
Dacogen™ for Injection (DAC) contains decitabine, an analogue of the natural deoxyribonucleoside 2'-deoxycytidine.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events were hematologic: neutropenia (90% vs 72%), thrombocytopenia (89% vs 79%), anemia (82% vs 74%), and febrile neutropenia (29% vs 6%); common nonhematologic events included pyrexia (53%) and hyperglycemia. 8 of 83 Dacogen-exposed patients discontinued for adverse events versus 1 of 81 on supportive care (83 of the 89 randomized patients were exposed to Dacogen).
